title: North Programme — Obligation Graph Schema
status: empirical schema with symbolic crosswalk kept separate
purpose: Give the North Programme a clean representation for banks, debt, contracts, guarantees, pensions, taxes, procurement, funding and other obligations while preventing symbolic karmic debt from being confused with material financial or legal claims.
design_rule: Obligation is an edge, not a mood. Every empirical obligation must identify the parties, mechanism, direction, legal/economic basis, value where observable, date, jurisdiction, source and confidence.

epistemic_firewall.empirical_obligation: A documented financial, contractual, statutory, fiduciary, institutional or operational duty between identifiable actors.
epistemic_firewall.symbolic_moral_obligation: A project-defined ethical or spiritual claim about harm, consequence, restitution or repair.
epistemic_firewall.crosswalk: The two may be compared as relationship structures, but one never proves or automatically creates the other.
epistemic_firewall.42T_rule: The project's approximately 42T karmic/spiritual balance must never populate amount fields in empirical finance records unless an independently documented material transaction exists.

edge_schema.relationship_type: bond | loan | deposit | guarantee | pension | tax | procurement | grant | subsidy | contract | lease | equity_commitment | trade_payable | insurance | treaty_commitment | security_commitment | regulatory_duty | infrastructure_service | other

principal_or_value.value_type: principal | market_value | committed | paid | exposure | estimate | not_applicable

edge_schema.basis: contract, statute, bond terms, budget act, procurement award, treaty, regulation, ownership agreement or other identifiable mechanism
edge_schema.status: proposed | authorized | active | partially_fulfilled | fulfilled | overdue | disputed | restructured | cancelled | unknown
edge_schema.jurisdiction: country / EU / treaty / contractual jurisdiction or null
edge_schema.seniority: senior | subordinated | secured | unsecured | statutory | not_applicable | unknown
edge_schema.conditions: covenants, milestones, triggers, eligibility or null
edge_schema.affected_groups: people, communities, firms, institutions or sectors materially affected
edge_schema.downstream_effects: known or hypothesized consequences if performed or breached

bank_node_schema.rule: A bank enters the graph through documented balance-sheet and institutional relationships, not through symbolic 'spiritual bank' language.

obligation_families.note: Represent only where there is a defined legal/institutional mechanism.

repair_crosswalk.empirical_failure_sequence: obligation -> nonperformance/breach/stress -> affected actors -> measurable loss/risk -> remedy/restructuring/intervention -> outcome
repair_crosswalk.symbolic_sequence: harm -> consequence -> moral obligation -> recognition/restoration -> repair
repair_crosswalk.shared_structure: Both concern relationships and consequences, but only the empirical sequence creates entries in financial/legal ledgers.
repair_crosswalk.use: This crosswalk lets the North synthesis discuss moral responsibility and material obligations together without collapsing them.

intervention_link.rule: A North Programme policy proposal should point to the exact nodes and obligation edges it intends to change.
